correctness.rationale: Exact unit-circle tangent area and beta gap density give the normalization. Conditional on one gap pi-delta, remaining normalized spacings are independent Dirichlet. Their residual tangent sum has tail O(r^{-(n-2)}), finite mean for n>=4, and truncated second moment O(log r) at n=4. Discarding residual above t^(2/3) has probability O(t^{-1-2(n-2)/3})=o(t^-2). On the good sector the unique threshold is delta*=2/t+2R0/t²+O((1+R0²)/t³), with expected error o(t^-2); integrating density q(delta)=q(0)(1+(n-2)delta/pi+...) and dividing by p_n gives exact C_n,D_n. Quadrilateral integration yields 12 log2/pi residual mean. Numerical checker independently confirms tangent intersections and diagnostic tail values, not the limit proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2014 primary theorem concerns large n and an externally truncated random polytope; 2023 Dirichlet extrapolations also take n to infinity. The geometric curvature–width theorem gives only the first-order fixed-n Pareto coefficient. Neither stronger model scope nor a known 1/t limit implies a 1/t² coefficient.

value.rationale: The first correction for the natural fixed-side-count tangent-polygon area distribution is an exact positive beta-weighted integral for every n>=4, not merely a special numerical example. The explicit quadrilateral logarithm and finite/infinite residual-moment boundary at n=3/4 describe a natural change of asymptotic regime and allow a quantitative finite-threshold Pareto-tail bias correction.
